source.title: Case report: a rare case of Hunter syndrome (type II mucopolysaccharidosis) in a girl.

confirmation.summary: Near-absent iduronate sulfatase activity with normal alpha-L-iduronidase, and a hemizygous IDS deletion.
evidence: a sharp decrease in the activity of iduronate sulfatase in the blood
Molecular genetic analysis revealed a hemizygous deletion in the IDS gene

note.text: Our daughter sat at nine months and walked at fifteen months, a little later than other children. From about eighteen months she stopped growing as she should, and her joints became stiff. Now, at four, she often complains that her legs hurt. A doctor told us her facial features look coarse. Urine tests showed she loses large amounts of certain sugar chains.
note.author: Peter's Kiro, written from the article's findings; not the parent's words

uncertainty: The girl also has Turner syndrome from a partial Xq deletion (46,X,del(X)(q22.1)); a ranker could reasonably return it. Only MPS II is the gold answer here.
